subject: Geo-redundant Dedicated commit options and SLA tradeoffs
messages:
From: Rachel Lowe <rachel.lowe@glowai.com>

Cc: procurement@glowai.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Pricing for geo-redundant Dedicated pools and DR options

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're preparing an internal budget and need concrete pricing and tradeoffs for Dedicated capacity in two scenarios:

1) Separate, mirrored Dedicated pools in US + EU (active-active with KV replication) — we want near-zero failover time and consistent latency across regions.
2) Primary (US) with cross-region failover (active-passive) — cheaper, but acceptable RTO up to ~15 minutes for non-critical workloads.

Questions we need answered:
- How do reserved commit discounts apply when we commit per-region vs committing globally?
- Is there a replication/DR surcharge for active-active? If so, how is it calculated (percent of commit, per-GPU-hour?)
- What throughput guarantees (tokens/sec, concurrent streams) come with a 12-month vs 24-month commit? Any penalties/credits for missed throughput?
- Are egress/replication network costs included or passed-through? Can we cap these in committed pricing?

For context, our current footprint (avg): 120k tokens/minute overall, spikes to 400k tokens/min, 95th percentile concurrency ~180 simultaneous sessions. Target p95 token latency under 200ms for US and EU users. We can share a capacity spreadsheet (attached) — please respond with a single-sheet summary of pricing options and a suggested default.

Attaching: GlowAI_RFP_multi-region.pdf (RFP summary)

Appreciate a response by EOD Monday if possible — procurement needs a ballpark for the Q3 budget.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Lowe
Head of Cloud Ops, GlowAI

Subject: Re: Request: Pricing for geo-redundant Dedicated pools and DR options

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear RFP and the capacity notes. Attaching a proposal and a simple capacity matrix so your finance/procurement team can run numbers quickly.

(Inline answers; see attached spreadsheet for line-item math)

1) Commit scope: commits can be scoped per-region or as a consolidated global commit. Per-region commits give you clear isolation and per-region SLAs; consolidated commits allow smoother pooling and typically yield a ~2-4% additional discount because of allocation flexibility.

2) Replication/DR surcharge: active-active (mirrored pools) requires replication of KV/state and a replication-capacity factor. We propose a replication surcharge expressed as a percent of the base commit: 12% per additional fully mirrored region (so US baseline + EU mirrored = baseline + 12% EU surcharge). Active-passive (cross-region failover) does not have a replication surcharge but does have warmup latency and potential cache-miss amplification on failover.

3) Throughput guarantees: tiered by commit length and committed GPU-hours. Example guarantees (illustrative):
- 6-month commit: baseline throughput SLO (no tail credits), best-effort autoscale
- 12-month commit: guaranteed sustained throughput baseline + 20% burst credits, p95 latency SLO commitments with service credits up to 5% of monthly invoice for missed targets
- 24-month commit: highest discounts and 30% burst credits, tighter latency SLOs and 10% service credits for misses

4) Egress & replication network costs: by default these are passed-through at cost, but for committed deals we can offer an egress cap or absorb up to a fixed monthly amount if you move to a 12+ month commit with a minimum baseline.

Counterpoints / options summary (attached):
- Option A (recommended conservative): Per-region commits with minimal replication for EU (active-passive failover), lower cost, acceptable ~5–15 min RTO for non-critical endpoints.
- Option B (recommended performance): Active-active mirrored pools US+EU, higher cost, consistent latency — replication surcharge applies. We included a blended discount example in the attached proposal.

Attachments: GlowAI_Dedicated_Proposal_v3.pdf, capacity_matrix_3-regions.xlsx

Next steps: happy to sync a short call Monday 7/13 — can Diego join to walk technical tradeoffs? Also looping Marissa to confirm discount bands.

Best,

Hi Rachel / Priya — quick technical clar to help procurement and infra teams: 

- Active-active replication: we replicate KV state and periodically checkpoint model-specific caches. This keeps tail latency consistent but requires double the working set on GPUs in each region (hence the replication surcharge). In practice, warm caches give sub-1s failover; fully warmed means p95 token latency differences are negligible.

- Active-passive failover: cold-cache penalty on failover can be significant depending on model context lengths; expect increased p95 token latency for the first 5–20 minutes post-failover unless you preload KV. We can provide a preload path but it consumes extra bandwidth/compute.

- Cross-region routing: our global routing policy supports weighted traffic and automatic fallback. If you want single logical endpoint (example: api.glowai.com) fronted by Redwood, we recommend regional DNS + Anycast + weighted push to minimize cross-region RTT. Note that cross-region routing introduces egress charging and additional headroom needs in the destination pool for sudden shifts.

- Throughput sizing: based on your numbers (95th ~180 sessions, 400k tokens/min peak), a conservative starting baseline is 3 x A100-equivalent GPUs in US, 2 x A100-equiv in EU for active-passive; if you go active-active mirrored, provision 4 x US + 3 x EU to avoid queueing during regional failovers and for buffer. See the attached capacity matrix for the math.

I'll join the call if you want to walk the matrix.

— Diego

Rachel — following Priya's note, a commercial offer from our side with flexibility to meet GlowAI's budget target. High level: 

- 12-month committed plan (GLW-2026-07): 20% base discount off list for the committed baseline (min GPU-hours agreed in attached capacity matrix).
- Replication surcharge: waived for year 1 if you commit to a two-region active-active baseline (we absorb the first-region replication surcharge as a one-time concession). Year 2 onward replication surcharge = 8% unless you increase global commit.
- SLA: 99.95% availability per region. Service credits: up to 10% monthly credit for SLA misses above threshold.
- Egress: we can include an egress cap of $8k/month in the committed pricing; any usage above the cap billed at-cost. We can convert this to a hard cap for legal if needed with higher committed dollars.
- Billing & procurement: standard Net30, with DocuSign for the SOW. I'll have legal prepare a redline-friendly version of the SOW once GlowAI flags preferred items.

If that aligns I can ask legal to draft the SOW + one-page amendment that shows the year-1 replication waiver and the egress cap. Priya — I'll coordinate a final number and DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
